title: input validate regex compiled without the standard timeout — catastrophic backtracking freezes the whole app on the UI thread
existing_state: The engine has a single source of truth for user-pattern safety — ScriptRegexDefaults.UserPatternTimeout (5s, Services/Scripting/ScriptRegexDefaults.cs:10) — and it is applied in ExtractCommand.cs:60 and ExpressionEvaluator.cs:98. InputCommand is the outlier: the user-supplied validate: pattern is compiled with new Regex(step.Input.Validate, RegexOptions.Compiled) and no timeout (Services/Scripting/Commands/InputCommand.cs:41), and IsMatch runs synchronously on the UI thread inside the dialog's OK handler (204-217, IsMatch at 209). A backtracking-prone pattern against a long pasted value hangs the UI thread indefinitely — and because ScriptPromptDialogRunner has already disabled the main form except the Stop button (which also lives on the now-frozen UI thread), there is no recovery short of killing the process.
recommendation: Add a factory on ScriptRegexDefaults (e.g. CreateUserRegex(pattern, options) that always passes UserPatternTimeout) and route InputCommand.cs:41 — and any future user-pattern compilation — through it; catch RegexMatchTimeoutException in BtnOk_Click and surface it as the validation error. Dropping RegexOptions.Compiled for a once-per-prompt match is a free bonus.
user_benefit: An innocent-looking validation regex can no longer hard-freeze the entire application mid-script with the main form locked; worst case the user sees a validation error after 5 seconds instead of reaching for Task Manager.

evidence.note: IsMatch executes in BtnOk_Click on the UI thread
UserPatternTimeout = 5s exists as the intended standard
extract applies the timeout — input is the inconsistent outlier
